content: The plasma concentrations of momelotinib may increase, potentially elevating the risk of adverse reactions when co-administered with erythromycin ethylsuccinate. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of montelukast by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate elevates nalemedine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Monitor nalemedine for potential adverse effects when co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir and neomycin PO via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the levels or effects of niacin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of nifedipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Initiate nifedipine at the lowest dose available if co-administered. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of nilotinib, nimodipine, and nintedanib via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition or CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. If adverse effects occur with nintedanib, management may involve dose reduction, therapy interruption, or discontinuation. Nirmatrelvir increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for increased erythromycin adverse effects, including QTc interval prolongation. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor for QTc interval prolongation and other adverse effects. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of nitrendipine and norgestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic concentrations of norgestrel, raising the risk of adverse effects. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and olodaterol inhaled both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Drugs that prolong the QTc interval may potentiate the cardiovascular effects of beta-2 agonists, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and osilodrostat both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and osimertinib both prolong the QTc interval. Periodic monitoring with ECGs and electrolytes is recommended for patients taking drugs known to prolong the QTc interval. Oxaliplatin increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by an unknown mechanism. Monitor for ECG changes if therapy is initiated in patients taking drugs known to prolong the QT interval. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of oxybutynin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and ozanimod both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Due to potential additive effects on heart rate, treatment with ozanimod should generally not be initiated in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs with known arrhythmogenic properties. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel and paclitaxel protein-bound by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of palbociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of paliperidone by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and paliperidone prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of palovarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration of palovarotene, a CYP3A substrate, with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the palovarotene dose by 50%. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the levels or effects of pantothenic acid by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of parecoxib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of paromomycin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and paroxetine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and pasireotide both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and pazopanib both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of pimozide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of pioglitazone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the effects of piperacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ponatinib increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of posaconazole by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the toxicity of pravastatin by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of prednisolone and prednisone by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are advised. Pretomanid increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by an unknown mechanism. Increased monitoring for drug-related adverse effects is recommended if pretomanid is co-administered with sensitive OATP1B3 substrates. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of propafenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the levels or effects of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and quetiapine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid use with drugs that prolong QT and in patients with risk factors for prolonged QT interval. Postmarketing cases show QT prolongation with overdose in patients with concomitant illness or with drugs known to cause electrolyte imbalance or prolong QT. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and quinine prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and quizartinib both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Monitor patients more frequently with ECG if co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of ramelteon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and ranolazine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Ribociclib increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of rifaximin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of rilpivirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by prolonging the QTc interval. Use rilpivirine with caution when co-administered with drugs with a known risk of Torsades de Pointes. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid repeating the rimegepant dose within 48 hours if co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of risperidone by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and risperidone prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of rivaroxaban by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Patients with renal impairment receiving rivaroxaban with drugs that are combined P-gp and weak or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may have significant increases in exposure compared with patients with normal renal function and no inhibitor use. Since these increases may elevate bleeding risk, use rivaroxaban in this situation only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of roflumilast by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with dual inhibitors of CYP3A4 and CYP1A2 may increase systemic exposure and result in increased adverse reactions. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of roflumilast topical by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and romidepsin prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the toxicity of rosuvastatin by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Rucaparib increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib and ruxolitinib topical by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of sacubitril/valsartan by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters. Co-administration with OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase valsartan systemic exposure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Sarecycline increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Monitor for toxicities of P-gp substrates that may require dosage reduction when co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of saxagliptin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of seladelpar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised in patients who are poor CYP2C9 metabolizers taking seladelpar and are co-administered a moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Selpercatinib increases the toxicity of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of sildenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider a starting dose of 25 mg in patients treated with erythromycin. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of silodosin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Sodium bicarbonate increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Sodium citrate/citric acid increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended.
